bib.title: Let's (not) just put things in Context: Test-Time Training for Long-Context LLMs

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Let's (not) just put things in Context: Test-Time Training for Long-Context LLMs". Rachit Bansal, Aston Zhang, Rishabh Tiwari, Lovish Madaan, Sai Surya Duvvuri, Devvrit Khatri, David Brandfonbrener, David Alvarez-Melis, Prajjwal Bhargava, Mihir Sanjay Kale, Samy Jelassi. Affiliations are Meta, Harvard, Kempner Institute, OpenAI, UC Berkeley and UT Austin. Several authors did the work as Meta interns. It is an arXiv preprint (2512.13898v1, cs.LG), 15 Dec 2025, with no venue stated.

COVERAGE: All 24 pages and all 74,643 characters were read, including the proof, FLOP, setup and result appendices. The extraction was clean.

MAIN CLAIM
- Long-context failure comes from "score dilution" in static softmax attention. Lemma 2.2 says that if m distractors score within Δ of the needle, then α ≤ 1/(1+m·e^−Δ).
- Lemma 2.3 says that keeping a fixed target mass 1−ε needs a target-minus-distractor logit gap of at least log((T−1)(1−ε)/ε), which is Ω(log T).
- Proposition 2.4 and Corollary 2.5 say a thinking token carries at most its own attention mass on the needle. Extra decoded tokens therefore cannot repair missing access to the evidence.
- The fix proposed is query-only test-time training (qTTT). It does one prefill to cache K/V, then takes a few gradient steps on W_Q only, using next-token loss on random spans of the context. The gradient is ∇q = (μ − k_j*)/√d_k, which moves q toward the needle. Lemma 3.2 says the margin rises by η‖∇‖².
- The theory is first-order and covers a single attention layer. It is a worst-case bound, not a measurement.

HEADLINE NUMBERS
1. LongBench-v2 with Qwen3-4B: average 27.0 for in-context, 33.5 for thinking and 39.6 for qTTT (Table 4, p21). The abstract's "12.6 points" is qTTT minus in-context (39.6−27.0).
   - Setup: six subsets, FLOP-matched, T_think=8192 against k=128 and N=32 qTTT steps.
   - Quote: "qTTT leads to massive 12.6% and 14.1% points improvements for Qwen3-4B on average across subsets of LongBench-v2 and ZeroScrolls benchmarks." (p1)
2. ZeroScrolls with Qwen3-4B: average 18.4 in-context, 23.9 thinking, 32.5 qTTT (Table 5, p22). That gives the 14.1-point gain over in-context. There are eight datasets.
3. Synthetic needle tasks with Qwen3-4B (Tables 2–3, p20): attention mass on the target and accuracy both collapse as context grows.
   - Bank transactions, thinking: accuracy falls from 36.0% at 512 tokens to 1.0% at 9,560 tokens. Mass falls from 0.46 to 0.04.
   - Under qTTT at 9,560 tokens, accuracy is 8.4% and mass is 0.25.
   - OLMo code bugs, thinking: accuracy falls from 50.0% at 512 tokens to 10.0% at 10,000. qTTT reaches 20.2% at 10,000.
   - At the shortest length qTTT is worse than thinking: 28.0 against 36.0 on bank transactions, and 45.7 against 50.0 on code bugs.
4. Matched baselines, Qwen3-4B (Tables 8–9): average on LongBench-v2 is qTTT 39.7, thinking 33.5, SC-8 36.6, SC-32 19.8. On ZeroScrolls it is qTTT 32.5, thinking 23.9, SC-8 28.2, SC-32 18.3. Splitting a fixed 8,192-token budget across more samples or beams hurts.
5. Latency (A100, Tables 10–12, p23–24): qTTT takes about the same wall-clock time as thinking. Prefill dominates; for 8B at 128k, prefill is 354 s and qTTT is 375 s.

QUOTES
- "all these methods generate additional tokens with the same static attention mechanism that is already under-allocating mass to the evidence." (p1)
- "Any successful inference-time strategy must change the similarity q⊤i kj (e.g., by updating queries) rather than sampling more tokens with unchanged parameters." (p5)

LIMITS
- Results are one run per configuration: "results are averaged over one run per configuration (low variance in our setting)" (p19). No confidence intervals are given. Sample sizes are never stated. Many LongBench-v2 scores are round numbers such as 26.0 and 30.0, which suggests small subsets.
- The learning rate is chosen per dataset on a held-out part of the validation set. Table 1 shows that high and low rates fail badly (for example 0.0% at 1e-4 on the longest bank-transaction context).
- The only matched baselines are thinking, best-of-n and beam search. Other long-context methods such as RAG, compression or other TTT variants are not compared. The authors list self-consistency inside the framework as future work.
- Gains are task-dependent. Summarisation gains are "smaller and comparable to thinking" (p9). Qwen3-32B shows qTTT below thinking on Long Dialogue History (75.5 against 77.9) and on GovReport (26.0 against 26.7 in-context).
- Only Qwen3 models of 1.7B to 32B were tested, and the synthetic contexts reach about 10k tokens. The 128k figures are latency only, not accuracy.
- The causal claim that dilution is "the primary" cause rests on the attention-mass correlation and a no-RoPE ablation. It does not rule out other causes.
- "Thinking" means Qwen3 /think mode, with sampled outputs.
- The paper itself says qTTT "Gains are task-dependent."
- The text says Figure 1c shows "more than 20%" gains, while the abstract gives 12.6 and 14.1 points averaged. Keep these two framings apart.

BUILDS ON
- Test-time training: Sun et al. 2020 (ICML), Liu et al. 2021 (TTT++, NeurIPS), Hardt & Sun 2024 (ICLR), Akyürek et al. 2024, and Sun et al. 2024 (TTT-RNN).
- Failure evidence: Liu et al. 2024 (Lost in the Middle, TACL), Hsieh et al. 2024 (RULER), Kamradt 2024 (needle in a haystack).
- Thinking baselines: Wei et al. 2022, Kojima et al. 2022, Wang et al. 2023 (self-consistency), Snell et al. 2024.
- Benchmarks: LongBench-v2 (Bai et al. 2023b) and ZeroScrolls (Shaham et al. 2023).

PROBLEMS: None. The PDF contains no embedded instructions. Text in the extraction is run together in places, for example "canconsumefar".
